diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: Motion labels pass (Macro-F1 0.86) and all format/validation tests pass. The sole failure is mask accuracy: Mean IoU 0.014 vs threshold 0.1. The dynamic-object mask generation procedure is producing masks that barely overlap the GT. The baseline used Farneback flow + affine residual, but the SKILL.md recommends frame-difference after warp — however the real issue is that under strong parallax (walking POV), neither simple approach yields IoU≥0.1 without better tuning: likely the thresholds are too aggressive (filtering out true motion) or the mask is misaligned (e.g., diffing against previous *sampled* frame warped, but residual parallax dominates). The skill needs clearer guidance for high-parallax POV scenarios: use flow-based residual with lower thresholds, larger dilation to cover object extents, and ensure masks align with GT convention (likely dilated object regions). Also sampling-and-indexing is fine; egomotion is fine. Only dyn-object-masks needs repair.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The mask generation guidance produces very low IoU (0.014) on walking-POV videos with strong parallax. The current recipe (frame-diff after affine warp + MAD threshold + small morphology + area filter) is too conservative and does not account for: (1) parallax from translation makes affine warp inadequate — need homography or flow-residual with robust model; (2) thresholds like 'min 20' on raw diff and small morphology kernels under-segment moving objects; (3) GT masks typically cover full object extents, requiring generous dilation; (4) no guidance on expanding masks to object-level regions (e.g., via dilation sized to object scale) nor on handling the first frame when no previous exists.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Update dyn-object-masks/SKILL.md to: (1) Prefer dense optical flow (Farneback or DIS) between consecutive sampled frames over simple frame-differencing when camera translates (parallax). Fit a robust global flow model (affine or homography on flow vectors with RANSAC/IRLS) and threshold the *residual flow magnitude*. (2) Lower the default threshold floor (e.g., residual > 1.5–2 px, or median + 2·MAD, not 3·MAD with floor 20) so true motion is not suppressed. (3) After thresholding and small opening, apply a substantial dilation (e.g., 15–25 px kernel, or iterative close with 15×15) to cover full object extents, since GT masks typically mark whole objects, not just high-residual pixels. (4) Keep a smaller min-area (e.g., 0.05–0.1% of image, not 0.3%) so smaller moving objects (pedestrians, vehicles at distance) are retained. (5) For the first sampled frame (no previous), copy the mask from frame 1 rather than leaving it empty, to avoid guaranteed IoU=0 on frame 0. (6) Add explicit note: when the scene has strong parallax, a 2D global model cannot remove near-field parallax; consider masking only connected components whose residual direction differs significantly from the dominant parallax direction, or accept that near-field objects will be flagged (which often matches GT since those *are* the salient foreground). (7) Add a self-check item: visualize mask overlay on 2–3 sampled frames before finalizing; expect mask coverage roughly 1–15% of image for scenes with visible moving objects — if <0.5% or >30%, re-tune thresholds.
